variable.name: Surface Temperature
variable.desc: Temperature of the Earth's surface skin — the layer a satellite actually sees, over land or ocean
variable.plain: The temperature of the very top of the surface — soil, leaves or water — the layer a satellite actually sees.
variable.trend_means: Rising means the ground or sea surface itself is heating, not just the air above it.

provenance.access: Automatic CMR discovery → authenticated OPeNDAP native-grid subset → local cache
provenance.aggregation: Native-cell polygon overlap × cos(latitude); at least 80% selected area each month
provenance.quality: Provider fill values/masks excluded; model reanalysis, not a direct measurement at every location

variable.name: Specific Humidity
variable.desc: Mass of water vapour per kilogram of air — actual moisture content
variable.plain: The actual mass of water vapour in a kilogram of air — the true moisture content, whatever the temperature.
variable.trend_means: Rising means the atmosphere is holding more water, which can feed heavier rain when it condenses.

provenance.access: Automatic CMR discovery → authenticated OPeNDAP native-grid subset → local cache

provenance.quality: Provider fill values/masks excluded; model reanalysis, not a direct measurement at every location

variable.name: Surface Pressure
variable.plain: The weight of the air pressing down on the surface.
variable.trend_means: Small swings track day-to-day weather; a long rise points to a change in large-scale circulation.
